correctness.rationale: The cototient identity \(c(x_i)=x_i-x_{i+1}+k\) telescopes to \(\sum_i c(x_i)=Tk\). Every cycle term is at least two, hence contributes at least one; a maximal term cannot be prime, and for composite \(M\) with least prime divisor \(p\le\sqrt M\), \(c(M)\ge M/p\ge\sqrt M\). Therefore \(\sqrt M\le Tk-(T-1)\). Equality forces all other cototients to be one and both composite inequalities to be equalities, hence \(M=q^2\) and every other term prime. Prime terms advance by exactly \(k-1\), and the return from \(q^2\) is equivalent to \(q=T(k-1)+1\). The inspected verifier independently checks the telescoping identity, bound, equality recognition and explicit periods 2, 3 and 4.

final_claim: Every minimal period-\(T\) orbit of \(F_k(n)=\varphi(n)+k\), \(k\ge2\), has maximum \(M\le[T(k-1)+1]^2\), with equality exactly for the prime-arithmetic-progression cycle ending in \(q^2\), where \(q=T(k-1)+1\) is prime and all preceding progression terms are prime.
limitations: One-step shifted Euler map with integer \(k\ge2\) only.
